A/B testing library, checked by simulation

  • Python
  • SciPy
  • pytest
  • CLI

Most A/B test tutorials stop at a t test, but real experiments break it in predictable ways. People check results every day, metrics are noisy, splits come out wrong, and dashboards track twenty metrics at once. I built a Python library that handles each one, with methods like CUPED and always valid sequential tests.

I tested every method on thousands of simulated experiments, then ran it on a real 90K player game test. It found a 4.3% drop in 7 day retention, and also caught that the groups were split unevenly.

Experiment Lab Run a real 90K player A/B test in your browser or drop in your own CSV. It walks through every step, from the split check to what checking it every day would have done. Open the lab

What it costs to turn off the internet

  • SQL
  • DuckDB
  • causal inference
  • Python
  • pytest

When a government shuts off a country's internet, there's no A/B test to run. So I built each country a synthetic twin out of 106 countries that stayed online, using GitHub's public data on how much code every country pushes.

Iran's blackouts in early 2026 cut its coding by 69%. Across six full shutdowns, every day offline cost about 1.3 days of work, so people didn't catch up after. First I planted 1,500 fake shutdowns to make sure the methods catch them.

Interactive Build a country's twin and see what simple comparisons get wrong Nine shutdowns from Myanmar to Iran, and how long one has to be before the data can see it. Open it

Trend following backtest

  • Python
  • pandas
  • SciPy
  • bootstrap
  • unit tests

A backtest of the 50/200 day moving average crossover on SPY, written from scratch with next day trades, trading costs and unit tests. I tuned it on 2000 to 2017 and tested on 2018 to 2026.

It didn't beat buy and hold. Then I checked whether picking the windows was just luck. Only 3 of 89 pairs beat buy and hold, and the probability of backtest overfitting came out around 0.57, basically a coin flip.

Household size prediction

  • Python
  • LightGBM
  • R
  • team of three

A class Kaggle competition, predicting how many people live in a household from their Amazon purchases. Since the answer is a small count, we treated it as classification and used the expected value of the predicted probabilities, which beat regressing on it directly.

TF-IDF on product titles beat our hand picked keywords, and with more features than rows we solved ridge in dual form. A stack of seven models placed 3rd of 23 teams.

Aura desktop widgets

  • Python
  • PyQt6
  • NumPy
  • Windows APIs

Desktop widgets for Windows. The main one shows the song that's playing and recolors itself from the album art, and the chrome text is rendered with NumPy. It only redraws what changed and pauses during fullscreen games, so idle CPU is close to zero.
